knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The executive summary is a one-page section placed at the front but written last. Break-even analysis and controls are later sections of the plan.

A regulated service should appear in the offer only after the licence or authority required in the state or territory is confirmed and held. The lesson does not grant any authority, so the learner must confirm the position from an authoritative source.
A projected growth rate is a target or an assumption. It needs a date, a reason and a review point. Calling it a fact or a market statistic overstates what is known.

practicalCriteria: Plan outline shows all ten sections in order, each with one sentence naming the decision it supports.
Every number in the outline is tagged as a fact, a target or an assumption, with a date or source.
Services list is checked against a written licence and insurance note, and any gap is marked out of scope.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80 per cent pass mark (all 3 of 3 correct for this lesson). A quiz pass is not verified practical competence. The plan outline is assessed separately by an assessor against the practical criteria.
evidenceRequired: Plan outline reviewed by an assessor against the practical criteria
stopWorkCriteria: Stop listing or offering any regulated service until the owner confirms the licence position from an authoritative source.
Stop any plan step that involves operating from a residence until council and insurance checks are recorded as done.
